back: A factor in the planning process considered to be true, real or certain, without proof or demonstration.
A limiting factor that affects the execution of a portfolio, program, project or process.
An uncertain event or condition that, if it occurs, has a positive or negative effect on one or more objectives.
A current condition or situation that may have an impact on one or more objectives. It has already occurred.

front: Risk vs issue in one question
back: Has it happened? No, it might: risk. Yes: issue.
Threat: a risk with a negative effect. Opportunity: a risk with a positive effect.
The project document that records all assumptions and constraints throughout the project.
The project document where information about issues is recorded and monitored.
The repository where outputs of risk management processes are recorded: identified risks, analysis, responses and status.
Scope, schedule and cost (the triple constraint), commonly joined by quality, resources and risk.

front: What happens when an assumption proves false?
back: It becomes a risk or an issue for the project.
A structure for describing a risk: because of X (cause), Y may happen (event), leading to Z (consequence).
The effect of uncertainty on the project as a whole. If too high, the organization may cancel the project.
Known-known (facts, not a risk); known-unknown (classic risk); unknown-known (hidden fact); unknown-unknown (emergent risk).
The degree of uncertainty an organization or individual is willing to accept in anticipation of a reward.
The measure of acceptable variation around an objective, reflecting risk appetite. Example: ±5% on cost.
An aggregate measure of the potential impact of all risks at a given point in time.
Avoid, mitigate, transfer, escalate, accept.
Exploit, enhance, share, escalate, accept.
Avoid: eliminate the threat or protect the project from its impact. Mitigate: reduce its probability or impact.
Shift the impact of a threat, and ownership of the response, to a third party. Examples: insurance, contracts.
Time or money in the schedule or cost baseline for known risks with active response strategies.
Time or money set aside by management in addition to the baseline, for unforeseen work within scope.
The approved version of a work product, changed only through formal change control and used for comparison with actual results.
Uncertainty: lack of understanding and awareness of issues, events or solutions. Ambiguity: being unclear, hard to identify causes, or many options.
The ability to absorb impacts and recover quickly from setbacks, including emergent risks and black swan events.
